task_spec: SUBJECT: Make a SOURCE conflict pick mean what the operator reads it to mean - the base collection's own entry carries the source's value for the divergent attributes - instead of transplanting the source's entry alongside base's and leaving two COLLECTION entries pointing at one LOCATION.

scope: traktor_nml/splice.py (_resolve_conflicts' source branch, assemble_output's pre-pass ordering), traktor_nml/textpatch.py (an entry-attribute patch beside location_patch), tests/test_splice.py, traktor_nml/README.md decision log, the gate repository's reconstruct fixture and serve script
scope: the /reconstruct page's SOURCE control keeps its wording and its behaviour becomes the wording (traktor_nml/gui/app.py may need no change at all - establish that rather than assume it)
out-of-scope: accessibility work of any kind - no screen-reader verification, no NVDA. Mouse and clicking is this version's bar
out-of-scope: the reconnect flow, its review step, and traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py's decision states - the model already carries base and source and needs no new state
out-of-scope: TODO.md's replace-playlist and the discovery gap
out-of-scope: the sibling traktor-nml-tool-plan repository, frozen at plan-final-w004 - this plan carries no code_changes and no waves
constraints: MUST: reconcile with the splice module docstring's own scope note, which states the base input is authoritative for its own COLLECTION and its bytes are never rewritten, and with DL-007's separation of byte-span assembly from attribute patching. This plan changes what that note claims, so the note and the decision log must be brought into agreement rather than left contradicting the code

MUST NOT produce two COLLECTION entries sharing one LOCATION - DL-004 forbids two entries pointing their playlist references at one LOCATION, and the served gate run on 2026-08-31 produced exactly that
MUST: every guard is made to FAIL first, and its docstring records the specific mutation applied and the specific output observed

MUST: a base input file is byte-identical before and after every run - the existing acceptance criterion from the reconstruction plan still holds for the INPUT FILES; what changes is the OUTPUT's copy of base's entry
MUST: output line endings match the base file's own, preserved per file
MUST: new decisions continue from the current high-water mark in traktor_nml/README.md (DL-115 at the time of writing - re-read and confirm)
MUST: documentation describes the code as it stands - no 'previously', 'now does', 'no longer', 'added'

MUST: a served-page gate run from C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool-gate is the acceptance step for anything the operator drives (DL-084, DL-113), re-run over the conflict fixture with a SOURCE pick and the written output read back
MUST: app.py stays 100% CRLF (1538 CRLF, 0 bare LF); the tree is not uniform, so read and write with newline=''
MUST: deliver as docs/plans/2026-08-31-source-resolution/ with plan.json and context.json
MUST NOT: regenerate the parity manifest or the gate fixture; never restore a file with git checkout
SHOULD: the suite runs under the SYSTEM interpreter, currently 446 passed / 3 skipped, not .venv
entry_points: traktor_nml/splice.py:_resolve_conflicts - the source branch: `if resolution == "source" or base_member is None:` picks a winner from the non-base candidates and appends it to new_entries. When base_member is None that transplant is correct; when a base record exists and loses, it adds a duplicate entry rather than changing base's

traktor_nml/splice.py:assemble_output - new_entry_texts transplants each winner's ENTRY span verbatim; the reconstruction pre-pass below it already rewrites base_source in memory and re-parses before any span is consumed (DL-096), which is the precedent and the place an entry patch would run

traktor_nml/textpatch.py:apply_text_patches, ElemPatch, location_patch, primarykey_patch - attribute substitution inside opening tags with every other byte preserved; location_patch is the shape an entry-attribute patch follows
traktor_nml/splice.py:_TRACKED_ATTRS - artist, title, album, filesize, playtime_float, bitrate: the attributes a divergence is measured over and therefore the ones a source pick must carry across
traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py - already projects BASE and SOURCE per group and hands splice a resolutions mapping; likely unchanged by this work
tests/test_splice.py - the nine per-key resolution guards, including the ones that assert the source record's attributes appear in the output and do NOT assert base's are gone
C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool-gate/reconstruct_fixture.py and serve_reconstruct.py - the fixture and serve script that found this; untracked at the time of writing
rejected_alternatives: Offer only BASE on the conflict screen - nothing can produce a broken collection, but the useful half of the control is gone; held as a stopgap rather than the destination

Make SOURCE redirect playlist references only and leave the COLLECTION alone - no duplicate entries, but the attribute the operator was shown and chose does not change, so the control does not do what its label says

Delete base's ENTRY span and transplant the source's - reaches the right end state but changes base's entry identity and its position in the collection, and discards any base attribute the source does not carry

Route the source pick through write_nml_safely or a full re-serialisation - splice is span assembly; DL-007 separates the two paths and the reconstruction plan states reconstruction must stay on the span path
current_understanding: symptom, measured on a served gate run: a SOURCE pick on a track present in both collections writes an output whose COLLECTION holds FOUR entries where base held three, with two of them carrying LOCATION /:Music/:two.mp3 - one ALBUM 'Base Album', one ALBUM 'Source Album'

the playlist's PRIMARYKEY for that track resolves ambiguously against both entries, and the redirect that would disambiguate is a no-op because the primary key is derived from the location, so base's key and the source's key are the same string

root cause: the source branch routes through the keep-first/keep-last picker, which until this change only ever ran when NO base record existed, where transplanting the winner is correct. With a base record present and losing, the transplant adds rather than replaces
why no guard caught it: the M-002 guards assert the source record's attributes appear in the output, which they do, and never assert base's are absent

the mechanism the fix needs already exists: textpatch.apply_text_patches substitutes attribute values inside opening tags with every other byte preserved, and the reconstruction pre-pass already rewrites base_source in memory and re-parses before any span is consumed (DL-096)
BASE picks are correct today and produce a clean output - only the SOURCE direction is affected

everything else in the conflict flow is verified working by the same gate run: the rows, both sides' values, the outstanding count, the bulk actions, an explicit pick surviving a bulk action, the refusal naming the count, and a clean write once every group is settled
assumptions: Patching base's ENTRY in place for the divergent attributes only - rather than for every tracked attribute - is what the operator means by picking source, since the divergent set is what they were shown (M) - the plan should decide this explicitly
An attribute present on the source record and absent on base's entry needs a stated rule: inserted, or left absent (M)
The conflict report's resolution token for a source pick stays 'source' and needs no new vocabulary (H)

traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py and traktor_nml/gui/app.py need no change, because the mapping they produce is unchanged and only splice's reading of 'source' changes (M) - establish by reading, not by assuming
invisible_knowledge: The splice module docstring's scope note is a v1 tradeoff record, not a physical law: it says the base input is authoritative for its own COLLECTION and its bytes are never rewritten. The reconstruction work already rewrites base_source in memory for playlist nodes, so the note is already narrower in practice than it reads
output is None exactly when errors is non-empty - SpliceResult's documented invariant; a partial write is not a shape this module has
old_to_new_key holds only keys a resolution actually redirected; a key with no mapping passes through as the raw key rather than erroring (DL-101)

The primary key is derived from the location, so two entries for one file cannot be told apart by key - which is why a duplicate entry is not merely untidy but makes the playlist reference ambiguous (DL-004)
Serving the page is the only gate that has ever caught a defect in gui/, and it caught this one after a green 446-test suite (DL-084)
Apply patches from FILES written as BYTES then git apply; capture git diff as BYTES and decode UTF-8 explicitly - subprocess(text=True) decodes via cp1252 here
The gate fixture for the reconnect flow is committed and must never be regenerated; the /reconstruct conflict fixture is separate and new
